description: Byte-exact WebTransport reliable-stream transcript for PROTOCOL.md section 15. Each record is canonical unsigned-LEB128 message length, one kind byte restating the WebSocket text, binary, or close opcode, plus the unchanged WebSocket message bytes. Records four and five are the ambiguous pair: identical valid-UTF-8 JSON bytes carried once as a text data-event and once as an opaque binary application payload (section 1.4), so a decoder that ignores kind provably cannot tell them apart. Record six is an empty text message, whose zero length is a complete prefix the kind byte still follows. Records seven and eight are a draining server's reconnect advisory and its close record, the last record that direction carries before FIN. fragmentLengths deliberately split the first record's prefix, kind, and body across separate reads, place a read boundary one byte before the first record ends, coalesce later records, end one read on the empty record's prefix and the next exactly where that record ends, and split the close code across two reads; a decoder delivers each record in the read that completes it. validRecords are single-record streams ending in FIN for edges the transcript cannot hold. Each invalidPrefixes and invalidRecords entry names the check that refuses it, and checks says what each check means; each invalidRecords entry is a complete stream ending in FIN. Entries marked dependsOnReceiverLimit can have a different verdict at some other receiver limit, and every unmarked entry holds at every limit of 125 bytes or more; entries marked assumesReceiverReadsOn hold for a receiver that reads on after a close record. reportsCode is the close code a receiver of that stream reports: the first close record it read (1005 for an empty one), or 1006 when the only close record is refused as malformed.

records.note: Byte-identical to the preceding text record. As binary its leading byte 0x7b is not a registered appendix C.3 tag, so section 1.4 delivers it to the application untouched; only kind separates the two records.
An empty WebSocket text message. Zero is a complete length, the kind byte still follows it, and the record delivers an empty message exactly as WebSocket does.

The close that follows the reconnect advisory (sections 3.9, 15.4): the WebSocket close payload, a big-endian code then a UTF-8 reason. It arrives after the advisory because it is an ordinary record, and its sender FINs after it.

checks.non-canonical: section 15.1: the length prefix is not the shortest encoding of its value
checks.over-cap: section 15.1: the prefix runs past 5 bytes; refused at the sixth byte at the latest, and MAY be at a fifth byte that still has its continuation bit set
checks.over-limit: section 15.1: a well-formed length above the receiver limit; judged before the kind byte
checks.unknown-kind: section 15.1: a kind byte other than 0x00, 0x01 or 0x02
checks.invalid-text: section 15.1: a text record whose bytes are not valid UTF-8 as a whole
checks.close-payload-length: section 15.4: a close payload of one byte, which holds no code
checks.close-code: section 15.4: a close code outside 1000-1003, 1007-1014 and 3000-4999
checks.close-reason-length: section 15.4: a close reason longer than 123 bytes
checks.close-reason-utf8: section 15.4: a close reason that is not valid UTF-8
checks.after-close: section 15.4: any byte after a close record on its direction, decided before any prefix verdict, by a receiver that reads on; one that stops reading after the close sends STOP_SENDING with NO_ERROR instead, and either way the close it read stands
checks.fin-inside-record: section 15.1: the direction finished while a record was incomplete
